newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-RAIN DISRUPTS ANOTHER DAY AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAIN DISRUPTS ANOTHER DAY AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: The Wimbledon tennis championships were disrupted by rain again on Friday.
The 1000 GMT start on the outside courts was put back indefinitely as heavy rain, which washed out Thursday's programme altogether, continued to fall on the All England Club.
Despite the overcast skies and continuing downpour organisers were optimistically predicting that play on the showcourts would start on time, at 1100 GMT.
Rain has spoiled all but one of the first five days of the Grand Slam tournament, leaving organisers more than 120 matches behind schedule.

Tournament referee Alan Mills said on Thursday that officials would have to consider emergency measures such as extending the tournament into a third week, reducing some rounds of the men's singles to the best of three sets or playing on the middle Sunday, traditionally a rest day.
The men's doubles competition, which has yet to get underway, has already been reduced to the best of three sets for the first three rounds.
Friday's weather forecast said there was a chance of drier weather in the afternoon and evening.
Natalia Zvereva of Belarus and Elena Likhovtseva of Russia were due out first on Centre Court in a bid to complete their first-round match which started on Wednesday.
Court One, if the rain stops, will see the eagerly-awaited Wimbledon debut of American teenager Venus Williams, touted as the next big name in tennis. She plays Pole Magdalena Grzybowska.
